title: Pathfinder: lightweight instrumentation gateway for cross-service trace routing
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Build a tiny, runtime-agnostic instrumentation gateway (Pathfinder) that lives in SDKs and edge middleware to normalize incoming request metadata, attach stable trace envelopes, and route traces into the platform with minimal overhead. Pathfinder is intended to be a single place to apply sampling hints, map legacy header variants to the canonical trace envelope, and emit a compact internal span header for downstream services. The goal is to reduce end-to-end tracing gaps and sampling skew across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments while keeping per-request overhead below 120 microseconds on common SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: SDK and middleware libraries include Pathfinder hook that transforms legacy headers (x-redwood-trace, baggage, traceparent variants) into the canonical 'x-rw-trace' envelope
End-to-end trace continuity for a synthetic cross-service flow shows >=99.5% span stitching at p99 latency without increased request latency above 120 microseconds on our Node and Go SDKs
Pathfinder honors sampling hints from clients and produces consistent sampling decisions across 3 deployments (hosted, dedicated, private) in test harness
Automated unit and integration tests cover header normalization, deterministic sampling decision, and back-compat fallthroughs
Docs and migration guide published to internal Confluence and SDK README with code snippets and roll-forward steps
tasks: Design header envelope and canonical key names
Implement C library shim for Rust/Go core that can be invoked from each SDK
Add Node and Go middleware that invokes Pathfinder on request ingress and egress
Add feature flag to console to opt in/opt out Pathfinder for a customer
Create synthetic cross-service test harness and golden trace comparison script
Write migration guide and release notes
comments: 2026-02-20 Miguel Torres: Kickoff sync complete. Decided canonical header will be 'x-rw-trace' with base64 compact envelope. Follow-up: Aisha to prototype Node middleware and Ilya to sketch C shim ABI.
2026-02-27 Aisha Khan: Prototype Node middleware implemented. Measured microbenchmarks show ~85us added on cold start and ~35us steady-state. Pushed initial PR for review.

2026-03-01 Code review (SRE): raised concerns about header size when baggage is large. Action: Pathfinder will only forward a 256-byte hashed baggage summary; full baggage sampling available asynchronously via logs.
2026-03-05 Ilya Petrov: C shim ABI finalized. It exposes normalize_headers(), sampling_decide(seed, hints), and pack_envelope(). Uploaded RFC in drive.

2026-03-09 QA: Synthetic flow tests show 99.7% stitching for 5-service chain at p50/p90; p99 shows 99.2% due to one edge case where legacy 'trace-id64' arrives without parent-id. Added fallback mapping rule.
2026-03-11 Product review (Sara Lee): Approved migration docs pending a small wording update around privacy controls. Console opt-in flag requested for first few customers.

2026-03-12 Performance note (Aisha Khan): Node e2e harness with 10k RPS shows Pathfinder increases tail-latency by ~0.7ms at p99 in worst-case headers; we will add an opt-out path for strict-latency customers
monitoring_query: promql: sum(rate(pathfinder_normalize_duration_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(pathfinder_normalize_duration_seconds_count[5m])) by (sdk) - use to alert if avg normalize > 0.00012
rollout_plan: Stage 0: feature flag off in console for all customers; enable in internal test orgs
Stage 1: enable for 5 canary customers with opt-in via console; monitor stitching and latency dashboards for 72 hours
Stage 2: gradual 10%->50%->100% rollout per region if canaries stable
Stage 3: publish migration guide and SDK release notes; open a support playbook
notes: Trade-off: tighter envelope reduces header size but makes debugging harder; agreed to include deterministic hash and preserve a short sampling trace id for troubleshooting
Fallback for unsupported clients: if Pathfinder headers absent, the middleware should attempt best-effort header translation from known legacy variants
Long-term: consider adding a small cached key-value store in runtime to avoid repeated normalization on hot paths
